# University of the Andes (Colombia)
The University of the Andes (Universidad de los Andes or Uniandes) was founded in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón and intellectuals from Colombia’s traditional parties as the country’s first nonsectarian and politically independent university. Its foundation was motivated by the nation’s urgent need for skilled professionals to support rapid industrialization and economic modernization during the Liberal Republic era. Modeled after American universities, Uniandes aimed to provide a liberal education alongside technical training to develop leaders capable of contributing to Colombia’s development. The university opened classes in 1949 with 80 students, emphasizing political neutrality despite Colombia's increasing political violence and establishing early programs such as the three/two program in cooperation with U.S. universities, fostering international academic exchange.
Organizationally, Uniandes is a nonprofit corporation governed by a Board of Trustees, Board of Directors, a Rector, Vice-Rectors, an Academic Council, and Deans leading 14 academic units comprising 10 faculties and several specialized centers. Its mission emphasizes pluralism, academic excellence, and ethical training, aiming to foster social and civic responsibility. The university’s campus in Bogotá blends renovated industrial and religious buildings with modern facilities, including extensive libraries, laboratories, and sports centers. Uniandes maintains broad international exchange programs with over 119 universities in 34 countries. Its student body is highly selective, with 95% of undergraduates from the top 1% of Colombian high school graduates. Notable alumni include former presidents, ministers, academics, artists, and scientists who have contributed significantly to Colombia’s political, cultural, and scientific spheres.
